anchor.exact: In Ainu, aspect is basically expressed by complex predicates made up of combinations of the conjunctive particles kor and wa and the existence verb an/oka(y).

anchor.exact: In most dialects there is a contrast between progressive aspect and resultative aspect.

anchor.exact: Syntactically, the complex predicates expressing aspect can be said to have originally been formed of adverbial clauses.

anchor.exact: In addition to these, forms made up of combinations of conjunctive particles and such verbs as ‘go’, ‘come’, ‘end’, and ‘not.exist’ are found as complex predicates related to aspect.

statement.ja: 接続助詞と oman「行く」、ek「来る」、okere「終える」、isam「ない」などの動詞との組み合わせも、アスペクトに関わる複合述語として見られる。

entailment.quote: In addition to these, forms made up of combinations of conjunctive particles and such verbs as ‘go’, ‘come’, ‘end’, and ‘not.exist’ are found as complex predicates related to aspect.

anchor.exact: Also, verbs like ‘go’ and ‘end’ are sometimes used like auxiliary verbs without conjunctions

anchor.exact: In Ainu, evidentiality is expressed by complex predicates composed of combinations of nominalizers and verbs.

statement.ja: 証拠性の複合述語において、補文は存在動詞の主語に対応する場合と、コピュラの補部に対応する場合がある。
